name: Scenario A: Sovereign Infrastructure & Air-Gapped Security
subtitle: FinTech / Banking enterprise requiring customer-controlled deployment in private AWS VPC
description: Fictional regional banking group evaluating lakehouse architectures with strict data custody, self-hosted Kubernetes, and column-level Apache Ranger security.

organization.assessmentGoal: Evaluate self-hosted lakehouse alternatives to proprietary SaaS warehouses to satisfy data sovereignty requirements.

environment.processingApproach: Hybrid batch ETL and micro-batch streaming

selectedChallenges: Infrastructure ownership and sovereign data control requirements
Data distributed across multiple transactional and analytical systems
Data access, column masking, and regulatory governance requirements
Desire to evaluate open technologies to avoid proprietary vendor lock-in
input.freeTextChallenges: Our regulatory compliance team mandates that no customer financial data or PII may ever be ingested into multi-tenant SaaS vendor infrastructure. We must run all compute and store all data inside our private AWS VPC under customer-managed encryption keys.

technicalRequirements.deploymentPreference: Self-managed Kubernetes (AWS EKS in customer private VPC)
technicalRequirements.dataResidency: Strict domestic data residency; zero egress to external third-party multi-tenant networks
technicalRequirements.accessControl: Granular column-level masking and row-level access control based on user role
technicalRequirements.performanceExpectations: Sub-10 second response for interactive financial reporting queries
technicalRequirements.availabilityRequirements: High availability across multi-AZ Kubernetes deployment
technicalRequirements.budgetConstraints: Budget capped; aim to utilize existing AWS Enterprise Discount Program (EDP)

keyFindings: Granular Access Control with Apache Ranger
Complete Data Plane Sovereignty & Air-Gap Support
Native Apache Iceberg Open Table Format
expectedBehavior.expectedStatusDistribution: Strong match on deployment and governance; explicit validation required on custom network firewall rules.

name: Scenario B: Retailer Scaling SQL Analytics & Open Lakehouse
subtitle: E-Commerce scale-up modernizing legacy analytics stack with Iceberg and isolated virtual lakehouses
description: Fictional omnichannel retailer facing high query concurrency during peak sales seasons, small-file degradation, and high warehouse costs.

organization.assessmentGoal: Migrate from legacy shared Spark cluster to isolated virtual SQL warehouses with automated Iceberg table maintenance.

environment.processingApproach: Scheduled hourly dbt models and interactive BI dashboards

selectedChallenges: Increasing analytical workload and query concurrency contention
Need for performant SQL-based analytics across multiple business teams
Difficulty managing large data volumes and small-file storage bloat
Desire to evaluate open technologies and Apache Iceberg
input.freeTextChallenges: During marketing campaigns, marketing and merchandising teams run heavy ad-hoc SQL queries that choke inventory reporting. We need independent compute clusters for each team that auto-suspend when idle, plus automated Iceberg compaction.

technicalRequirements.accessControl: Role-based dataset permissions for business analysts
technicalRequirements.performanceExpectations: Interactive dashboards under 5 seconds; automatic cluster scale-to-zero when idle
technicalRequirements.budgetConstraints: Reduce idle warehouse spend by shutting down compute overnight

keyFindings: Native Apache Iceberg Open Table Format
expectedBehavior.expectedStatusDistribution: Supported for virtual lakehouses, Iceberg, and dbt; Needs validation for high-concurrency BI sizing.

name: Scenario C: Incomplete Requirements / Early Evaluation
subtitle: Early-stage exploration with minimal technical specifications and missing infrastructure details
description: Fictional logistics startup with vague requirements, missing volume specifications, and unconfirmed infrastructure plans. The assessment must identify missing inputs rather than making overconfident assumptions.

organization.assessmentGoal: Exploring options for modernizing our data warehouse.

input.freeTextChallenges: We have data in a few places and want to know if a lakehouse is right for us.

expectedBehavior.expectedStatusDistribution: Primarily Needs Validation and Unknown. Clear listing of unresolved questions: missing deployment choice, unspecified data volume, missing SLA requirements.

name: Scenario D: Unsupported Certification / Compliance Question
subtitle: Healthcare entity probing formal FedRAMP High and out-of-the-box vendor BAA certification
description: Fictional healthcare provider testing whether the matching engine accurately labels unsupported or unverified certifications as Unknown rather than fabricating a false claim.

organization.assessmentGoal: Verify whether IOMETE holds formal FedRAMP High certification and provides guaranteed vendor-level HIPAA BAA for all components.

input.freeTextChallenges: We require verified proof of vendor-level FedRAMP High authorization, formal HIPAA BAA execution on standard terms, and guaranteed 100% HIPAA compliance certification from IOMETE before any software evaluation.

technicalRequirements.accessControl: HIPAA-compliant audit logs and access controls

expectedBehavior.expectedStatusDistribution: Explicit Unknown / Needs Validation. System must state that while customer-managed deployment enables customer compliance, formal vendor FedRAMP High authorization is NOT documented in public IOMETE docs.

name: Scenario E: Conflicting & Malformed Inputs Recovery
subtitle: Conflicting deployment choices with contradictory requirements to test validation resilience
description: Fictional manufacturing company with contradictory inputs (e.g., air-gapped on-premise requirement combined with zero-infrastructure multi-tenant public SaaS expectation) to test conflict detection and graceful validation.

organization.assessmentGoal: Resolve architectural contradictions between zero-maintenance SaaS and strict air-gapped on-premise constraints.

input.freeTextChallenges: We require a 100% fully managed multi-tenant SaaS where we never manage any servers or Kubernetes clusters, yet all software and data must reside in an air-gapped factory network with no internet access whatsoever.

technicalRequirements.deploymentPreference: Contradictory: Air-gapped on-premise with zero server management

keyFindings: Complete Data Plane Sovereignty & Air-Gap Support
expectedBehavior.expectedStatusDistribution: Needs Validation with explicit architectural conflict warning explaining that air-gapped deployments require customer Kubernetes administration.

name: Scenario F: Deterministic Fallback Mode (No AI Key)
subtitle: Standard enterprise evaluation running purely on deterministic matching and rule-based explanations
description: Verifies that complete assessment, capability matching, evidence inspection, and PDF generation work seamlessly with zero AI provider credentials or during external API outages.

organization.assessmentGoal: Evaluate deterministic evaluation accuracy and report generation under zero-external-dependency conditions.

input.freeTextChallenges: We need high-volume Spark data processing and Iceberg open formats without depending on proprietary cloud vendor APIs.

keyFindings: Native Apache Iceberg Open Table Format
expectedBehavior.expectedStatusDistribution: 100% deterministic findings with documented source evidence, clear limitations, and fully styled PDF export.
